name: Acme Security Summary Q4
summary: This summary combines the results of the Q4 portal test, the external exposure review and the red team exercise. The business should act first on the exposed access key, the customer data access flaw and the lack of monitoring of VPN sign-ins.

scope.rules_of_engagement: No denial-of-service. Business hours only. No real customer data.

findings.title: Secrets exposed in a public code repository
findings.description: A cloud access key was found in a public code repository.
findings.impact: A cloud account key was public. Anyone could have used it to reach company data until it is revoked.
findings.remediation: Revoke and rotate the exposed secrets, remove them from history, and add secret scanning to the development workflow.

findings.title: Insecure direct object reference (IDOR)
findings.description: The invoice endpoint does not check who is asking.
findings.impact: Any customer could read other customers' invoices, which is a data protection risk.

findings.remediation: Enforce object-level authorisation on every request on the server side and avoid relying on hard-to-guess identifiers as protection.

findings.title: Lateral movement not detected
findings.description: Remote access and file activity is not monitored.
findings.impact: An attacker could move through the network for days without anyone noticing.
findings.remediation: Improve endpoint and network telemetry, tune detections for remote service use and rehearse the response.

findings.title: Missing HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS)
findings.description: A browser hardening setting is missing on the public website.
findings.impact: Users on hostile networks may be downgraded to unencrypted HTTP.
findings.remediation: Send Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains once all subdomains support HTTPS.

recommendations:
1. Rotate exposed secrets this week.

2. Fix the invoice access flaw before the billing release.

3. Fund 24x7 monitoring of VPN and file server activity.
